# FitToll

> An app blocker that charges a physical toll. When you open an app you've
> blocked, FitToll takes the screen first and asks for push-ups or squats,
> counted by your camera. Pose detection reads real joint angles, so the reps
> have to be real. Everything runs on the device — no video is recorded and
> nothing is uploaded.

FitToll is available on iOS (16.0+) and Android (8.0+). Developed by Aurobindo
Gupta. Tagline: "Pay the toll to scroll."

## How the exercise gate works

- Pose detection runs on-device: Apple Vision on iOS, Google ML Kit on Android.
  It works in airplane mode.
- The counter tracks joint angles, not motion — shaking the phone, waving at the
  camera, or tapping the screen produces no reps.
- Half-reps do not count. A rep requires the full range of movement.
- Push-ups add a hip-angle form check at the bottom, which distinguishes a
  push-up from a sag. Squats calibrate to your body and distance at the start of
  every session, and offer a front view (counts reps) or side view (counts reps
  and checks form).
- Three strictness levels: Beginner, Intermediate, Pro.
- Each unlock is a fixed window of real time, counted from the moment the app
  unlocks. Closing the app does not pause it and unused minutes are not saved.
  Each app has its own window.
- There is no skip button. There are three emergency bypasses per day; each one
  doubles the reps for that app on the next unlock, the doubling clears only
  after a clean unlock, and spending all three resets your blocking setup.

## Pricing

- Free: block one app, both exercises (push-ups and squats) at all difficulties,
  15-minute unlocks, last 7 days of stats.
- Premium: $5.99/month or $29.99/year. Lifts the one-app limit, allows longer
  unlock durations, and shows the full 90 days of stored exercise history.
- Exercise sessions are deleted from the device after 90 days on both tiers.

## Privacy

- Camera frames are processed on-device and discarded. No images, video, or pose
  data is transmitted or stored.
- FitToll does not track which apps you use beyond detecting that a blocked app
  was opened, and does not collect location, contacts, or health data.
- On Android, app detection uses the Usage Access permission
  (`UsageStatsManager`). FitToll does not use an Android Accessibility Service.
  On iOS it uses the FamilyControls / Screen Time API.
